tests.name: refund under 100.00 on a recent order is approved automatically
tests.rule: Criterion 1
tests.setup: order placed 10 days ago; refund request of 99.99; decision step only, provider send not invoked
tests.expected: decision is automatic approval; no manager wait recorded

tests.name: refund of 100.00 waits for a manager
tests.rule: Criterion 2 (boundary)
tests.setup: order placed 10 days ago; refund request of 100.00
tests.expected: status is awaiting manager; not approved

tests.name: refund of 150.00 waits for a manager and is not approved by the decision step alone
tests.rule: Criterion 2
tests.setup: order placed 10 days ago; refund request of 150.00
tests.expected: status is awaiting manager; no approved status

tests.name: refund of 10.00 on an order 91 days old is refused
tests.rule: Criterion 3
tests.setup: order placed 91 days before the request; refund request of 10.00
tests.expected: status is refused; no approved status

tests.name: refund of 10.00 on an order 89 days old is approved
tests.rule: Criterion 3 (inside the limit)
tests.setup: order placed 89 days before the request; refund request of 10.00; fixed clock

spec_findings: Criteria 1 and 3 conflict for a refund under 100.00 on an order older than 90 days: criterion 1 says approved automatically, criterion 3 says refused. The spec must state which rule wins.
Criterion 3 does not say whether exactly 90 days is refused (time-of-day or day granularity). No test freezes that boundary.
Currency, decimal precision and the comparison basis (before or after other adjustments) are not stated.
Criterion 4 does not say what happens when the provider refuses or fails, or whether a manager-approved refund is re-checked against the 90-day rule.
covered: Criterion 3 for an order 91 days old and one 89 days old
not_covered: Criterion 4: sending the approved refund to the provider and storing the confirmation id. The recorded decision forbids stubbing the provider client here and there is no sandbox, so this cannot be tested under the current rules.
Assertion that a pending or refused refund never reaches the provider, for the same reason
Exact 90-day boundary (spec silent)
Conflicting case: under 100.00 on an order older than 90 days (spec conflict)
escalate_reason: Criterion 4 cannot be tested under the recorded decision that forbids stubbing the provider client with no sandbox. The decision owner must allow a test double at the provider boundary or provide a sandbox. The spec conflict between criteria 1 and 3 also needs its owner.
actions_now: Write the decision tests for criteria 1 to 3 without calling the provider. Escalate criterion 4 and the criterion 1 versus 3 conflict to the decision owner.

tests.setup: order total 200.00; one code worth 10 percent

spec_findings: The spec says 'a discount code' (singular). It does not say whether several codes may apply to one order, whether the largest or the sum applies, or what happens with an unknown or expired code. The spec owner must decide before any multi-code test is written.
covered: Single code applied to the total
not_covered: Several codes on one order (behaviour unspecified, so not frozen)
Unknown or expired code
escalate_reason: The implementer wants the largest-of-two behaviour locked in, but the spec is silent on multiple codes. The spec owner must decide. QA will not freeze unspecified behaviour in a test.
actions_now: Write only the single-code test. Refer the multi-code question to the spec owner and do not add the implementer's test.

tests.setup: each agent role in turn; a document in reviewed status
tests.action: attempt the approved transition through the gate the design must provide
tests.expected: refused; audit entry names the actor; status unchanged. Blocked: the gate does not exist yet

tests.name: the owner's transition to approved is recorded with the owner as writer
tests.rule: Binding: owner-only transition, and the writer is recorded

tests.action: owner performs the transition through the gate
tests.expected: status is approved; audit entry names the owner. Blocked: the gate does not exist yet

spec_findings: The binding does not say how the owner is identified on a write.
The spec does not require an audit record of the writer on status changes.
defects: Every role process writes the status field of docs/*.yaml with fs.writeFile, with no choke point and no record of the writer. This is a design defect, seen in the scenario description, not run.
not_covered: The property itself: the design has no point at which the owner's transition can be enforced or tested
A static scan can be bypassed by dynamic paths, so it is a partial check only
escalate_reason: The property cannot be met by the current design. The architect and implementer must add one status-change gate that records the actor. QA cannot test a transition that has no function to call.
actions_now: Write the target tests now, marked blocked until a single gate exists. Escalate the design defect to the architect and implementer.
